title: Crepuscule shift annotated playbook — 2026-09-23
content:
Shift window: 2026-09-23 19:00 UTC -> 2026-09-24 03:00 UTC
Shift alias: Crepuscule (EU–NA overlap)
Primary takeaways (high level):
- One medium-severity partial degradation event for hosted API in eu-west region during peak handoff. Root cause suspected: aggressive KV cache eviction triggered by a background reclaim job following a model rollout; combined with a latent autoscaler reaction for dedicated pools.
- Failover behaved correctly: routing policy sent ~12% of traffic to secondary region until cache warmed; latency spike contained to ~8m for majority of requests.
- Runbook gaps surfaced: the cache-reclaim step and its coupling to model rollout are not clearly documented; autoscaler grace settings ambiguous for dedicated pools.
- Several follow-ups created (owners assigned). See "Action items / Follow-ups" section.

Incident timeline (concise):
- 19:42 UTC: CloudWatch/Prometheus alert ALERT_API_P99_HIGH_EU triggers (p99 > 500ms over 2m). Initial pager to SRE.
- 19:44 UTC: Oncall (Priya) acknowledges. Slack thread created: #sre-ops: "eu p99 spike, investigating".
- 19:46 UTC: Error rate for generation endpoints remained low (<0.5%); however tail latency rose dramatically. Grafana shows cache hit ratio falling from 0.94 -> 0.55 over 3 minutes.
- 19:47 UTC: Observed a Kubernetes CronJob (reclaim-kv-cache) completed a run on serving-runtime-nodes-eu with concurrent small model rollout (model v1.8.3 -> v1.9.0 canary) triggered 19:45.
- 19:48 UTC: Manual check of recent deploy: rollout shows 20% of pods on new image; rollout job annotated with "reclaim=true" (unexpected).
- 19:50 UTC: Executed temporary routing override to increase traffic to eu-secondary for latency-sensitive routes. (command: rwdctl routing set-policy --region eu-west --fallback-region eu-secondary --policy latency-priority)

- 19:52 UTC: Reached out to platform-eng channel; confirmed reclaim job is intended but should not run during canary rollouts.
- 19:58 UTC: Started a controlled restart of 6 affected serving replicas to clear inconsistent KV state. Command used: kubectl -n serving rollout restart deploy/serving-replica --selector=canary=true -l zone=eu-west (note: restarted only canary pods).
- 20:05 UTC: Cache hit ratio began recovering; p99 latency trended back toward baseline by 20:12 UTC.
- 20:20 UTC: Removed routing override at 20:18 after stability observed; monitoring remained green. Incident classified as medium; no customer-facing page required.

Mitigation steps performed (detailed):
1) Isolate traffic to fallback region for latency-critical routes (rwdctl routing override) — minimal config, low blast radius.
2) Restarted canary-serving replicas to flush inconsistent KV state introduced during reclaim.
3) Temporarily increased cache-liveness TTL for KV store for eu nodes (kvctl set --region eu-west --ttl 300s) — reverted later to normal after warm-up.
4) Coordinated with platform-eng to pause reclaim cron for 30m (manual toggle on cron controller).

Observed metrics (before/during/after):
- p99 latency (eu generation endpoints): baseline ~210ms -> spike ~820ms -> recovery ~230ms
- cache hit ratio: 0.94 -> 0.55 -> 0.89
- CPU on serving-nodes-eu: small bump from 60% -> 75% during warming, normalized to 63% after recovery
- error rate: unchanged (below alerting threshold)

Hypothesis / root cause notes:
- The reclaim job aggressively evicted KV cache shards without coordinating with ongoing canary pod starts. When canary pods came up, they suffered cold cache and sequential token fetches led to tail latency amplification.
- Autoscaler for dedicated pools uses a CPU-based heuristic; because the load pattern was steady and not CPU-heavy, autoscaler did not add capacity quickly enough to absorb cold-cache penalties.
- Lower-level kernel/network metrics show no packet loss; storage latency for KV store remained within SLOs. Not an infra networking issue.

Runbook gaps identified (actionable):
- "serving-runtime/kv-reclaim" cron should have a safety window preventing runs during canary/rollouts. Add preflight check to skip when rollout.active=true label present.
- Add a specific play in the serving-runtime runbook: "if cache hit ratio drops >20% concurrent with a rollout, pause reclaim, increase TTL, and warm cache on new pods" with exact commands and verification queries.
- Document routing override commands and rollback steps in the Global Routing runbook (we used rwdctl ad-hoc flags). Current docs reference old CLI flags.
- Autoscaler config for dedicated pools should include a memory/KV-warmth signal or add a cooldown/fastpath for scale-up on tail-latency triggers.

Action items / Follow-ups (owners & due dates):
- PLAT-2291: Add preflight guard to kv-reclaim CronJob to check rollout labels (owner: Marco Ruiz, due: 2026-09-30)
- SRE-312: Update serving-runtime runbook with cache-warm play and exact commands + verification dashboards (owner: Priya Nambiar, due: 2026-09-26)
- PLAT-2297: Review autoscaler triggers for dedicated pools; evaluate adding p99 latency as a scale-up signal (owner: Dana Lee, due: 2026-10-07)
- DOCS-88: Global routing runbook update to include rwdctl examples and rollback steps (owner: Technical Writer team, linked: CONFLUENCE-OPS-4821, due: 2026-10-02)
- Follow-up postmortem draft (owner: Priya Nambiar, co-author: Marco Ruiz) — aim to publish internal postmortem by 2026-09-29.

Emergency checklist (quick):
- Acknowledge alert
- Scan cache metrics: grafana dashboards -> "serving.kv.hit_ratio"
- If hit_ratio < 0.7 and p99 > threshold: execute routing override to fallback region
- Pause reclaim cron: kubectl -n serving patch cronjob reclaim-kv-cache --patch '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
- Restart affected replicationsets selectively: kubectl rollout restart with selector canary=true
- Increase cache TTL temporarily: kvctl set --region <region> --ttl <seconds>
- If scaling needed: escalate to platform-eng pager (pagertoken:PLAT) and run: rwdctl capacity request --pool dedicated --region <region> --reason "tail-latency warmup"

Notes to oncoming shift (hand-off specific):
- Watch for regression after scheduled nightly model rollout at 02:00 UTC — platform-eng plans another minor model push; ensure kv-reclaim cron is still suspended around that time until preflight guard is in place.
- If you see p99 spike without error rate increase, check kv hit ratio first, then recent rollout annotations.
- Slack breadcrumbs: thread #sre-ops "eu p99 spike" pinned messages contain commands used and logs.
- Dashboard panels added during shift: quicklink -> Grafana "serving/runtime - crepuscule view" (pinned on ops home).

Post-incident retrospective notes (brief):
- Positive: routing fallback semantics and rwdctl tooling allowed for a quick mitigation with low customer impact.
- Negative: automation (reclaim cron) lacked cross-component awareness; safer defaults would have prevented the cold-cache storm.
- Risk: identical pattern could occur during any canary on other regions; recommend rolling out preflight guard globally.

Miscellaneous operational notes / TODOs for runbook authors:
- Include sample queries for verification: promql for hit ratio and pod-level cache misses (include example aggregation).
- Add exact kubectl selectors we used to avoid accidental restarts of non-canary replicas.
- Consider making kv-reclaim a Job that takes a "maintenance-window" annotation rather than a global CronJob.

Unresolved questions (for platform-eng sync):
1) Why did the deploy pipeline annotate canary with reclaim=true? Was this an intentional safety flag or an accidental propagation?
2) Is there a reason autoscaler currently omits p99 latency signals for dedicated pools?
3) Can KV store provide a per-shard eviction watermark metric to allow smarter cache reclaim heuristics?

Contact list (oncall/tier2):
- Platform eng: Marco Ruiz (pager), Slack: @marco.ruiz
- Serving runtime lead: Dana Lee, Slack: @dana.lee
- Database/KV: Rahul S. (oncall), Slack: @rahul.kv

Final handoff note:
- I'm handing over to night oncall, @Anika Shah, at 03:00 UTC. All mitigations reverted to normal except PLAT-2291 which remains open. If anything spikes, follow the emergency checklist and escalate to platform-eng immediately.

-- Priya Nambiar (oncall), Crepuscule shift 2026-09-23
